question: One major EU project to enhance our security and defence involves optimising military mobility within the EU. That aspect of our security policy is addressed in various documents, such as the Strategic Compass, the EU-NATO declaration and in the Commission’s specific action plans on military mobility, further harmonisation of all aspects of military mobility occupying centre stage in this connection. Now that the Action Plan on Military Mobility 2.0 is one year old: 1.

Can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy (VP/HR) provide an update on the implementation of that action plan, which, as was announced, was to be submitted by November 2023?
Will the VP/HR put forward new initiatives on military mobility by 2026?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.4.2024) On 13 November 2023, the High Representative/Vice-President and the Commission submitted to the Council and European Parliament a Joint Progress Report on the implementation of the Action Plan on Military Mobility 2.0 from November 2022 to October 20231. The comprehensive implementation of the Action Plan on Military Mobility 2.

02 will be the main focus of work until 2026 at EU level. This includes in particular the identification of the main corridors for short-notice and large-scale movements of military personnel and materiel in case of a conflict or for military exercises, and the identification of gaps in the infrastructure on those main military mobility corridors, that should be mitigated as per priority.

Complementary to the Action Plan, the European External Action Service and Commission services are currently engaging with the Member States to develop and adopt a renewed ‘military mobility pledge’. This renewed pledge would build on the first pledge undertaken by Member States in 2018, in the context of the first EU Action Plan on Military Mobility.

The renewed pledge would incorporate new developments on military mobility in light of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and would set out measures for improvements at the national level, in coherence with the overall objectives of the Action Plan on Military Mobility 2.0.
